answer_1.quote: We present initial experiments with two controllable text generation (CTG) methods that aim to control the stance of automatically generated replies.
answer_1.outputs: Generated chatbot replies (responses) with controlled stance and offensiveness attributes.

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the responses generated by all the candidate conversation models using the following automatic metrics, Distinct-1,2 is the ratio of unique unigrams and bigrams to the total. % Bad is percentage of generated responses containing profane word/phrases... % Off is percentage of responses predicted offensive... % Agree, % Neutral are percentages of generated responses predicted agree or neutral respectively.

answer_4.quote: We conduct in-house human evaluation of 4 models: DGPT baseline, Blender bot, DAPT neutral stance control and ATCON both control... For every model response, we investigate its plausibility {Yes, No}, stance towards the last comment in the thread {Agree, Disagree, Neutral}, and offensiveness {Yes, No}.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators assess each model response for plausibility, stance, and offensiveness.
